Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
The Sect War event proved very popular, and two new factions were
introduced to handle the overflow players (Black Hand and Kindred Most
Wanted). Twenty six players played, with the finals taking the top 5
players regardless of starting team, as there were 7 teams. Two
Imbued made the finals, and the three vampire decks made a pact to out
them first. After an hour and forty minutes, an unblocked
Conservative Agitation ousted them both, and then the vampire decks
played until time without another oust. Many players commented on the
enjoyment of the cooperative deck building, even going so far as to
state that it was the most fun portion of the day. The Laibon team
officially won the tournament, with Adam Hulse's Akunanse gaining 1.5
VPs in the final to allow his prior round 4 place seat to put him
above the KMW Gangrel Antitribu of Hugh Angseesing and the Brujah
antitribu of 3rd Edition piloted by Matt Strehlow.

A large number of players played in the last chance qualifier, but
that was in a completely separate room, so I will let LSJ or one of
the finalists report on that event.

Oscar managed to round up 20 players for a draft that started drafting
around 7 pm as well. That was still going on when I left for the
night.

See you Saturday for day 1 of the North American Continental
Championship.

http://www.TheLasombra.com/NAC2006/

The seating was Josh Duffin (Imbued), me, Hugh, Alex Ek (Imbued), Adam.
Josh was top seed and I was second going into the finals. If the other
vampire playing players were planning a let's take out the Imbued first
and then fight it out ourselves, I was planning a stab in the back
right before the Imbued ousting (working the same sort of lines as
let's all kill Nergal, oops, I killed my prey before Nergal died).
Instead the other vampire playing players wanted to do a let's split
the prize box evenly amongst us no matter how it turns out (well,
provided the Imbued didn't win). An early Creepshow Casino helped me
get some additional stealth to get past the Imbued's easy +1 intercept,
not so easy to get more. Also, no one expects Alacrity (especially from
the 3 cap). I had lots of fun calling KRCs for 2 pts to my grand prey
and 2 pts to my predator. A Rein's of Power really helped us win,
adding back a much needed 6 pool to all the vampire player's reserves
and even hit the Imbued players for 1 damage each. Like The Lasombra
said above, I was able to take out both Imbued players in the same
action with a Con Ag, since they were at 2 and 3 pool, unfortunately I
had Hugh as my prey, so I got 0 vps for that. All in all the format was
lots of fun, playing for my 3rd Edition team each round (you didn't
have to sit at a table with your own team) and then playing for the
vampire team in the finals. I hope to play this format sometime again
in the future, but the large number of players required to build
several teams (and then not sit with your team at a table) and the
unsanctioned aspect of it make me think I might be waiting awhile for
the chance.

Later,
~Rehlow

Messages.Author: witness1
Messages.Body:


Indeed. I think the format was probably biased toward the imbued from
the beginning, in spite of not having starters.

In two boxes of NoR, we had roughly 3.5 of each rare, 10 of each
imbued, and 20 of each common. The NoR distribution was much smoother
than several other sets, and we got 4 Churches, 4 Champions, 4 Crusader
Swords, and 4 Living Wood Staff.

We seriously considered putting Break The Code, Edge Explosion, and
Recalled to the Founder into one of the decks.

I'm pretty sure Duffin and Alex had "less-than-60-cards" because of the
conviction effect. I was the only player to go up to 90 (and it was a
mistake).

The rules cards were really good - "Dude! You just got outpressed by
Boxed In!" We had an Info Highway and a Sudden Reversal each, 3 Barrens
between us, and 3 Elder Libraries as well. We also got a total of 8
Fake Outs, which meant I didn't have to hog them for my Cleave deck.
There were also a couple of magnums. 5+ Angels of Berlin apiece meant
sufficient out-of-turn equipping. Even Dodge was key.

Cleaving Count Germaine for 8 with a Living Wood Staff and pressing
when he soaked was fun.

Witness1
-believe the lie

I didn't play Imbued in any of the constructed events before NAC Day 2.
Because they're too good. That was sort of validated in my Day 2
experience, in that I was not ousted in rounds 1 or 2 (playing a fairly
standard Defense/Judgement master-heavy deck), but got only 0.5 VPs each of
those rounds; in round 3 I was ousted (with 2-3 of the other 4 players
working on me) but only about 5 minutes before time was called. My presence
in each game seemed to cause great concern that I would become unstoppable
if I were allowed to build up for longer than, say, three turns. Luckily I
was able to talk people out of giving away my VP to their prey/new
predator/etc in two of the three rounds, but unluckily I was not able to
oust anyone before time while we all did that much talking (and thinking).

On a side note, the Sect War finals that became "3 vamps vs 2 imbued" was
pretty fun and seemed reasonably fair - since it was already a kind of team
event, playing the finals as teams was an interesting change from "normal"
tournament finals. Unfortunately both of us imbued got off to kind of a
slow start and couldn't handle being outnumbered. Probably we should have
sat back-to-back but didn't take into account (before choosing seating) just
how much it was going to become a vampires-vs-imbued affair.

Josh

Messages.Author: witness1
Messages.Body:


This is interesting, as throughout the tournament I never thought that
the right answer for any table was to gang up on me, and for the most
part they didn't.

Day 1, game 1, I got my first VP because my grandprey KSed backwards
after being bled intensely by my prey, and worked that strong position
into a 4-VP game win.

Game 2 I sat in front of weenie presence, who sat in front of Ravnos
Are Kholo, who sat in front of !Malk stealth bleed. My Tzimisce prey
had no worries from me, though had I played better I could have held on
for a half a VP. Yay.

Game 3 I got hit cross-table for something like 6 KRC points from my
grandpredator. It was a stupid move on his part and we both got ousted
quickly. Yay.

Day 2, game 1 I sat behind Tupdog-Nephandus, who killed and
pillow-faced two of my imbued, something like a net 10-pool investment.
Luckily, Jennie was the survivor and managed to get 2 Flak Jackets, a
Leather Jacket, Hide and Vigilance, so she never got destroyed. I was
also able to credibly threaten a self-oust if my last minion was
removed (which would have put Giovanni powerbleed behind the Tupdogs,
which he feared more than my Laptop). I nearly got a whole VP, but I
wouldn't have gone any farther.

Game 2, my potence-combat predator could have crushed me had he acted
about 3 turns sooner, and I knew it. He didn't believe it, though, and
decided to backoust Robyn instead. I used the Darby Dance (Laptop +
Leather Jacket + Vigilance) to oust my prey and stay untapped (out of
Harass range), but only got that VP because my predator and grandprey
killed her minions instead of mine. Once that was done, they dealt me
off the table, and 3 anarch revolts (plus bleeds of one) killed me.

Game 3, my predator was Tzimisce block-combat. My prey ended up with my
first Magnum on Maris Streck (I decided letting him have it was better
than blocking him and letting my predator have it). My prey was a
Huitzipochtli + Maris + IC deck, and he made a 3-2 deal with his
grandprey fairly early. The only reason I had a chance at a VP is that
I was able to credibly threaten an out-of-turn self-oust (which would
have screwed up the deal, by forcing a VP and 6 pool on my predator).
Had I played better I would have ended up with an actual VP (maybe 2,
depending on time).

Of course, I've already confessed that the Heart of Nizcehtus was the
only thing holding my crappy deck together, so maybe I'm the blind man
here.

Witness1
-believe the lie.

Messages.Author: Jay Kristoff
Messages.Body:
Tobias wrote:

> Congrats on this win, Jay!

Thank you.

> Could you describe how your tables went and how you and your deck dealt
> with them?

Round 1

Me (Gargoyles)
Bill Troxel (Nos breed and vote)
Connor Bell (Giovanni and Le Dinh Tho)
Grim (Muaziz with Ferox)
Johannas Walch (Krassamir with Euro-Brujah)

Connor opens with Le and pops cards from Grim's hand.
Bill is making Embraces and 3rd Trads. and has vote control.
Grim is watching his hand, then his pool get violated.
Johannes shows some combat, but is aslo quick to pull
the Legendary Vampire Krassamir out of combat with my Gargoyles.
Johannes has Carver's in play.
I get Stone Dog, Heidelburg Castle, and Dragonbound.
Bill ousts Conner, and nearly gets Grim.
My two S.D. rushes a turn against Bill's weenies, coupled with Carver's
wreck Bill.
Johannes makes 25-30 blood from Carver's.
I eventually oust Bill.
I tell Grim that we should team up to oust Johannes, then fight for the game
win.
Grim says no.
The three of us play it straight for a while.
I am getting the short end of the stick as Grim's bleeds get bounced into
me,
and one of my Hatchlings is stuck in torpor from Carver's.
Johannes eventually ousts me.
I tell Grim he played poorly. (using other language)
With very little time left, Grim torps out Johannes and earns the Game Win.
I take back every thing I said to him.
Grim: 2 VPs, Bill: 1 VP, Jay: 1 VP, Johannes 1 VP

Round 2

Me (Gargoyles)
Mindy Bell (Stanislava and other dom/PRO folks)
Unhappy guy (wennie pre)
Nat Hammond (Gangrel with Torvus Bloodbeard)
John Bell (Guruhi swam with embrace and many "..are the Land")

Sorry for not knowing the unhappy guy's name.
He was unhappy because John was coaching Mindy throughout the game.
I encouraged the unhappy guy to get used to it.
He did not.
Nat wasn't able to go forward much all game as his predator(s) kept him
busy.
John cranks out Gurihi embraces before I have the int. to block them.
Mindy can have her way with the unhappy guy, and there's not much I can
do about it.
I decide that I also need to be John's predator (as well as prey) because
Nat is busy with weenie pre.
I play Dragonbound and try to torp as many of the Guhuri as possible.
Mindy ousts the unhappy guy.
John's final push into me leaves me with one pool before he is ousted
by my Dragonbound.
I recover pool with Blood Dolls, the Rack, and Club Zombie.
Mindy struggles to do much to Nat.
I get a Stone Dog and go to work on Mindy's vamps.
I play Jack and oust Mindy and Nat in order.

Jay: 3 VPs, Mindy: 1VP, Nat: 1 VP

Round 3

Me (Gargoyles)
David Tatu (Potence Settites with Stunt Cycle)
Christian Chénard (Kyasid toolbox)
Ben Swainbank (Enkidu)
Large Michigan guy (Lasombra bleed/vote)

Christian's deck had more combat in it than one would expect.
David got beat up by both Christian and me.
Enkidu rushed his predator and prey effectively.
I bled into David as my Lasombra predator was busy getting beat up.
Ben doesn't oust the Lasombra (possibly intentionally to put pressure on me)
Christian is beat up, and asks me why he should stay around if only to die
to me after I oust David.
I'm affraid of Ben's Enkidu combat.
Christain wants a deal where he gets two VPs (Ben and the Large Michigan
guy),
and I get three (David, Christain, and last player standing).
I agree to the deal because Christian's stealthy bleeds are the best way
I know of to get Enkidu off the table.
I oust David.
Christian and I team up to mess with Ben (I take Powerbase: Montreal from
Ben,
I rescue Christian's vamp, etc.)
The Lasombra guy gets a few votes and bleeds through to me, but I have a ton
of pool.
Time gets tight. I tell Christian I need the game win, and may have to oust
him if we run
get too close to the time out. (Christian is at close to no pool).
With very little time left, Christian ousts Ben and the Large Michigan guy
one after the other.
I then tell Christian that I am ready to accept his concession.
He concedes.

Jay: 3 VPs Christian: 2 VPSs

Final Round

I'm a little foggy on this, but I think I was the second seed going in.
I knew nothing of the decks of the other players.
I sat so that I was preying on Alex Harmon with David Zopf
as my predator, with Andreas Nusser across the table from me. (I think)
Steve Boyd-Bucy then sat as my prey.
The table looked like this:
Me (Gargoyles)
Steve Boyd-Bucy (Kindred Spirits stealth bleed)
Alex Harmon (FoS with Temptation)
Andreas Nusser (OBF/DOM stealth bleed)
David Zopf (Lasombra with OBF)

David had been Andreas' prey in an earlier round,
so he knew what was coming.
David tried to make pool with Creation Rites/Con. Boon.
He also bounced a bleed or two, but wasn't able to keep
up with the constant bleed pressure from Andreas.
David chose not to bleed me or vote pool damage to me
so as to not pave the way for Andreas (thanks again David).
Alex had his hands full as Steve pounded into him with K.S. bleeds.
I did nothing other than work a Blood Doll and make a Hatchling,
and get a Razor Bat.
Alex put Temptation on two of Steve's vamps and eventually
two of Andreas' vamps.
I torped one of Andreas' vamps after it was bounced to me.
Andreas ousted David.
Andreas then seemed to be low on stealth and having trouble getting
past my vamp with a Razor Bat.
When Alex was able to borrow the first of Steve's vamps with
Temptation, he sent it on the D action to burn my Mob Connections
(after removing all but one of its blood with his Heidelburg Castle.
I was happy to send Steve's vamp to torpor afer I blocked that action.
I played Dragonbound.
A turn or two later, thanks to Free States Rant and Temptation,
Alex and I again teamed up to torp another one of Steve's vamps
and two of Andreas'.
Alex helps me oust Steve with a KRC with the idea that I don't mess
with him until after he ousts Andreas.
That was fine with me.
In our heads-up match, I contest Heidelburg Castle, and get a Stone
Dog to rush his vamps.
Alex tempts both of my Hatchlings and uses them skillfully to
rescue his vamps and bleed me.
Even so, I had too much for Alex to handle.

Jay: 3VPs, Alex: 1 VP, Andreas: 1 VP

Thanks for your interest in the deck and my games.

Jay Kristoff



True. Against the rest of the table, they have little chance (as with any
deck). Of course, expecting the table to gang up against a particular
deck-type is one of the classic signs of a "broken" or "unbalanced"
archetype (since if a deck is balanced, it shouldn't require an entire table
to ally against it).

I, too, saw Break the Code played a bunch (even when no one on the table was
playing Imbued), but I don't think it's all that *effective* a piece of
anti-imbued technology. Granted, in the one game where it was played while
I *was* playing Imbued, I did get ousted, and the Break the Code did make at
least some contribution to that since (once it was played, relatively late
in the game) it was canceling out my Unmasking intercept which I needed
pretty often against my !Malk stealth-bleed predator. But I think the Break
the Code by itself would still not have come close to getting me killed, if
I hadn't also been receiving stealthy bounced bleeds from cross-table, if my
predator had had a normal amount of pressure from her own predator (instead
of zero pressure), or, indeed, if I had not played Fear of Mekhet on my
prey's Arika (costing me 2 pool) on my last turn before being ousted (I
played it in the expectation that I could then probably oust my prey on my
own next turn).

As long as players playing vampire-based decks can count on all the other
vampire-based-deck players at the table to work together to get Imbued decks
off the table, I think that's all the anti-imbued tech that people really
need. But can we count on that behavior to last forever? And is it
desirable as a method of "balancing" the imbued?

Josh

pretty definitely won't be playing imbued at the e.c.

If they have to ally against you to oust you, they shouldn't be allying
together to give someone else a VP. If they have to ally against you to
prevent you from winning, you're right about being unbalanced.

> I, too, saw Break the Code played a bunch (even when no one on the table was
> playing Imbued), but I don't think it's all that *effective* a piece of
> anti-imbued technology.

Break the Code is shit. It should require another Gehenna event in
play. As it stands, it's about the biggest effect-for-cost of any hoser
in the game (depending on whether you consider PTO a hoser). It costs
nothing to play. It doesn't even have a DNR clause. So now there's an
unburnable Haven Uncovered on all my minions. Great.

> Granted, in the one game where it was played while
> I *was* playing Imbued, I did get ousted, and the Break the Code did make at
> least some contribution to that since (once it was played, relatively late
> in the game) it was canceling out my Unmasking intercept which I needed
> pretty often against my !Malk stealth-bleed predator. But I think the Break
> the Code by itself would still not have come close to getting me killed, if
> I hadn't also been receiving stealthy bounced bleeds from cross-table, if my
> predator had had a normal amount of pressure from her own predator (instead
> of zero pressure), or, indeed, if I had not played Fear of Mekhet on my
> prey's Arika (costing me 2 pool) on my last turn before being ousted (I
> played it in the expectation that I could then probably oust my prey on my
> own next turn).

So, Break the Code didn't oust you, but how close did you come to
winning the game? It sounds like you almost made a VP. Yay.

So, if you can count on The Unmasking coming out, then Break the Code
only puts you back to neutral on intercept. It's only a free,
no-stealth, haven uncovered that lasts until the Break the Code player
is ousted.

But if there's no Unmasking in play, then you have to spend your
precious convictions just to block 0-stealth actions (like bleeds). And
you can't count on being able to take that many bleeds. Combine that
with the Haven effect and your important minion (Jennie) won't be long
for the world unless her Haven is Secured.

However, if it required a Gehenna event in play, I'd at least have the
strategic option of not playing the Unmasking to avoid the Haven
effect. It costs me the Edge Explosion, which could be problematic, but
there are times when it's definitely worth it.

> As long as players playing vampire-based decks can count on all the other
> vampire-based-deck players at the table to work together to get Imbued decks
> off the table, I think that's all the anti-imbued tech that people really
> need. But can we count on that behavior to last forever? And is it
> desirable as a method of "balancing" the imbued?

Maybe it's just that my playgroup is heavily into Animalism, but they
don't typically need that much ganging up to keep me from getting VPs.

Ousting me is hard for a lot of deck types, but ousting me crosstable
is rarely playing to win. Ousting me backwards is occasionally, but not
typically, playing to win.

At the NAC, it never took more than 2 players working together to oust
me (that only happened in one game). In the games where I was not
ousted, my predator was hampered either by an aggressively strong
predator of his own, or killed crosstable by Tupdogs. Without any table
ganging up on me, nor Break the Code played at any table, I was able to
earn 1 GW and 6 VPs over the both days.

I should of course consider that I'm not as good a player as you are,
and that my deck was crappy, but I just don't see the imbalance.

> Josh

> pretty definitely won't be playing imbued at the e.c.

Witness1

About Break the Code specifically, here's some thoughts: any deck with
Anthelios should probably add Break the Code and Emergency
Preparations. Anti-imbued tech, anti-Gehenna tech, untap-your-fatty
tech, and if all else fails, pitch-for-a-different-master with
Anthelios tech.

Similarly, a Mother of Horrors/War Ghoul deck with the Unmasking can
add a similar package.

It doesn't have to be Break the Code, of course. It could be any other
Gehenna event that suits you. But since BtC is so cheap and easy, and
nobody likes the imbued anyway, it's probably a good choice.
